how: Calls recruit flag builders, defenders and kindred city or sports rooms without establishing that every requested room answered.

statement: explaining how the canvas works during and after placement
how: Members explain pixel placement both to potential contributors and to people asking after closure.
A requested deep link makes the canvas fight findable without proving a later placement.
A volunteer promises their best and receives thanks in bare lines.
A defense call receives a direct bare commitment to join the fight.
A member proposes the flag and another member reports contributing in that thread.
Members propose and revise lettering, sports marks and additions instead of simply filling a fixed initial design.
Members report progress and perimeter work to the thread.
Coordinates, linked designs and a template guide the intended lettering.
The script Ohio lettering and its template do not establish scripts, bots or spare accounts placing pixels.

Proposing the flag and calling for hands occur in one initiating post rather than two demonstrated successive stages.
A posted design settles output only insofar as placers recognise the current target rather than restoring what others intentionally erase.
Visible consensus requests and references to leaders cannot resolve comparative prevalence or exclude formal decisions inside unseen chats.
Members seek local consensus before communicating a territorial proposal without thereby establishing a formal leader or voting rule.

statement: choosing a communication venue for planning
how: Flag builders and expansion proposers advertise Discord independently of any established interroom coalition.

Contributors prioritise defense and worry that divided attention will leave existing marks exposed.

Repair preserves intended work only when placers know which version the shared design now requires.
Contributors clarify exactly which mark should disappear before repairers switch to erasure.
Reported destruction warrants a stated need to relocate, while completed relocation and collective weighing of alternatives remain unverified.
The relocation passage names destruction, not a manpower judgment, as the reason for needing another location.
A neighbouring representative reaffirms a common border and receives a promise to expand elsewhere.
A participant explicitly presents themself as the neighbouring room's representative when reaffirming the border.
A member promises the neighbour will have no problems and locates possible expansion elsewhere.
Border talk receives promised restraint, but subsequent compliance by every placer is not demonstrated.
A request to repay earlier flag help receives a pledge of one pixel.
A member claims an alliance with an external chat without establishing its terms or sustained collective implementation.
An alliance claim and a newly created communication channel do not establish coalition formation caused by shared defensive strain.
Defense and neighbour border talk coexist without a cited statement that erosion by that neighbour triggered negotiation.
Shortage prompts requests to kindred rooms, but completed external help caused by those requests remains unverified.
The border exchange and the reciprocal help request involve different partners without an evidenced link between them.
Proposing to cede neighbouring rows does not establish that the room occupied a host's territory under the host's rule.
Seeking consensus and opposing territorial cession do not explicitly contest who may bind the room to an agreement.

statement: joking about a volunteer's best effort
how: A volunteer answers mock blame by distinguishing best effort from skill without establishing a pre-existing in-joke.
After placement stops, participants reinterpret the frozen mark to include three cities beyond its school association.

statement: continuing an ordinary aesthetic dispute after a prank
how: The skyline joke branches into disagreement over whether HDR looks bad or cool beyond the prank's reveal.

Recruitment and a sticky request do not establish that flooding prompted moderation or containment.
The completed work receives collective pride, thanks and credit for particular contributions.
Members record repairs completed before closure and mourn the last fix that closure prevented.
Contributors celebrate the completed work, while the record does not independently establish a report causing a later completion ritual.
Celebration and recording can occur in the same closing declaration rather than requiring distinct successive stages.
Accepting a residual pixel and wishing for more QA do not establish a dispute over cleanup of a shared historical copy.
Pride in a preserved achievement and a pre-close expansion invitation do not establish a successor activity or a decision to keep the collective.
Recording the finished work is visible without an evidenced transition to a future collective project.
Calls propose removing, recolouring or taunting rival marks without verifying every proposed attack was executed.
A proposal explicitly calls for replacing a neighbour's logo with a hockey mark.
A closing post claims the school got the last laugh and another commenter supplies a competing school interpretation.
The first visible canvas call already attacks a rival, so attack can initiate mobilisation rather than follow a separate earlier recruitment stage.

Acknowledging a maintenance recommendation does not demonstrate that the proposer ceased attacking or that the entire room accepted restraint.
The complete attack reply branch invokes numbers and maintenance rather than a truce or a border deal.
